**From:** {{< meta from-address >}}  
**Manuscript Location:** {{< meta manuscript-location >}}  

My dear [CC](../persons.html#329)
Tory is banished, [Juliette](../persons.html#870) fell in love with him, so he is gone to Witham Chase, a very good home for him, and Vic is left lamenting – The mother mews all over the place but as she did before Tory went, I think it is from native accidie, not maternal grief-[^2] [Aimée](../persons.html#869) brought [Miss Price](../persons.html#1209) to tea and sent Juliette, a little friend and a sort of semi governess to picnic on the top of the hill.

It was very pleasant –
Fancy the German hatred to the English so that an acquaintance would not bow to [Anna](../persons.html#195) in the theatre!

Aimée tried to explain the rights of the Boer war to a gentleman German but he would not listen for a moment.

Of course they were very happy at Ammergau.

They staid for the 2d performance on Whit Tuesday for the peasants Of course we could talk only chiefly of the terrible China - I suppose there are many more victims besides those given in the list of the Legation, and we do not know how many of the other nations.
I suppose Tientsin[^3] is safe for the present, but [Mrs Bishop](../persons.html#1817) tells of such splendid hospitals at Hanchow and Mukden One English doctor has been there 18 years. [Miss Finlaison](../persons.html#512) came home Friday night, very much done up.

It was influenza bringing on paralysis and apoplexy, and the niece Dora was very ill with that endless influenza, and Amy only just keeping about.[^4] What they are all to live upon I cannot think. [Mrs Barton](../persons.html#2235) continues to write and justify Irene for a childish freak
[Mary Morshead](../persons.html#28) and [Sister Sarah](../persons.html#466) come for a fortnight on the 27th. I wonder if [Mr Jacob](../persons.html#747) belongs to the [Bishop of Newcastle](../persons.html#748) There were some cousins, who I think lived in Guernsey A wife without children may be just the thing, but what a bouleversement[^5]
your affectionate

C M Yonge

[^1]: Printed up to ‘18 years’ by Coleridge, Life, 344-5, and dated 17 July 1900 The rest struck through with a line in the MS.

[^2]: Vic and Tory were cats.

[^3]: As a response to the ‘Boxer’ uprising in Peking on 20 June a six-nation force landed at Tientsin on 14 July, and relieved Peking on 14 August.

[^4]: Dora and Amy, who seem to have been Miss Finlaison\'s nieces, may possibly have been [Elizabeth D.

Jenner](../persons.html#759) and [Amabel Jenner](../persons.html#762).

[^5]: The Rev.

John Jacob had just been appointed Vicar of Tormohun.
